subject: Packaging construct + quantization scope checklist
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie@brightroute.ai>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightroute.ai
Date: 2027-12-05T17:12:00Z
Subject: Packaging for Optimize toolkit — initial scope and quant questions

Hi Elliot,

Thanks again for the demo last week — positive vibes here. We want to scope a short pilot of Redwood's Optimize toolkit: batching/caching recommendations + quantization guidance for our dialogue + retrieval workloads. Before we lock schedules, two quick asks so our procurement and infra teams can evaluate: 

1) What specific quantization tiers do you recommend for a 6B decoder model serving chat with 1k concurrent users (typical prompt length ~600 tokens)? Rough choices we saw in the docs (FP16 / int8 / q4* variants) — we need expected latency and quality tradeoffs at each tier.
2) On packaging: what’s in a pilot credits bundle (what features, what uplift vs. hosted rates), and do you include a measurable KV/prefix cache audit and suggestions as part of the pilot?

I attached our short requirements CSV. Procurement copied for timing.

— Sophie
BrightRoute, Head of Infrastructure
attachments: BrightRoute_requirements.csv (csv)
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie@brightroute.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-12-06T14:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Packaging for Optimize toolkit — initial scope and quant questions

Sophie — great to hear, thanks for the details. Short answers first, then a suggested pilot outline: 

Quantization tiers (high level):
- FP16 (baseline): best quality, typical latency for your profile ~+0–8% vs FP32 but higher cost. Good for final validation.
- INT8 (stable): ~20–30% cost reduction, ~10–25% faster in our runtime depending on kernels; marginal drop in some open models for rare token choices.
- Q4_K (aggressive 4-bit): ~40–60% cost reduction; large speedups for long-context workloads but you should expect occasional slight quality regressions on low-frequency tokens.
- Q4_x8 / mixed: often a good middle ground for chat-heavy signals; we can run a quick A/B on your prompt set.

Pilot packaging (what we include):
- $40k USD in pilot credits applied to hosted usage (covers inference + Optimize tooling).
- One 8-week engagement: KV/prefix cache analysis, 2 batching profiles (throughput and latency), and a quantization evaluation on a canonical prompt set you provide.
- Deliverables: quantization recommendation matrix (model/variant -> recommended quant), cost/delta sheet, and an implementation runbook with safe fallback policy.

I'll attach the Optimize playbook and a sample cost model worksheet for you and procurement.

Next steps: 30-min call to confirm the prompt set and decide the model variants to test (we recommend starting with the 6B and a 13B baseline). Is Thursday 10am PT OK?

Thanks,
Elliot Price
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
E: elliot.price@redwoodinference.com | M: +1 415 555 0134
attachments: optimizer_playbook_v2.pdf (pdf), cost_model_sheet.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie@brightroute.ai>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-12-07T09:42:00Z
Subject: RE: Packaging for Optimize toolkit — initial scope and quant questions

Hi Sophie — quick technical clarifications from ops/solutions side: 

1) Latency and quality expectations: for your workload (1k concurrent, ~600 tokens) we expect:
   - FP16: p50 generation latency ~220–260ms per 256-token chunk on T4/Infer-class; highest fidelity.
   - INT8: p50 ~160–200ms, small increase in hallucination risk on corner cases.
   - Q4 variants: p50 ~120–160ms; larger variance on very long prompts due to compression noise.

2) Caching & batching guidance we will run during the pilot:
   - Prefix cache audit: we’ll surface top 200 prefixes for reuse and estimate cache hit-rate uplift; typical enterprise customers see 10–25% token reduction from prefix caching alone.
   - Batching: we’ll test continuous batching windows (5–20ms) and a throughput-oriented batcher for off-peak windows. Expect 15–35% latency improvement with safe SLOs.

3) Data & evaluation: please share 250 representative prompt-response pairs (we’ll keep them private, deleted after the pilot unless you request retention). We’ll produce a short eval comparing top-1 outputs across quant tiers and include simple automated QA checks.

I’m attaching a short quant-guide with our recommended test matrix. Happy to walk through it on the call.

— Laura
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: quant-guide.md (md)

Thanks both — the technical notes are helpful. Procurement asks two follow-ups: 

1) Can you provide a worked example showing how the $40k credits convert to the hosted rates (we run a mix of chat + retrieval; estimate ~12M tokens per month during pilot)? A simple table that contrasts FP16 / INT8 / Q4 cost over 8 weeks would be ideal.
2) For the audit, will Redwood provide the raw hit-rate estimate and the projected monthly savings if we applied the recommended cache? We need that in the statement of work to sign off.

If you can send the short example table and a one-paragraph SOW-style statement including deliverables / timeline, procurement can review next week.

— Sophie
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@brightroute.ai
Date: 2027-12-09T15:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Packaging for Optimize toolkit — initial scope and quant questions

Sophie / procurement team — attached is a short worked example and an SOW paragraph. Summary here inline for speed: 

Commercial proposal (summary):
- Pilot: 8 weeks, $40k in credits (applies to hosted usage and Optimize tooling hours).
- Deliverables: cache hit-rate report (top-200 prefixes), quantization matrix & test artifacts, cost-delta worksheet, implementation runbook, one training session for your infra team.
- If BrightRoute signs a 12-month committed agreement within 60 days after pilot completion, Redwood will provide a 15% discount on committed inference spend for the first 12 months (exclusions apply).

Worked example (estimates for 12M tokens/month):
- FP16 baseline: estimated spend per month = $18,000 (pilot 8 weeks pro-rated).
- INT8: estimated spend per month = $12,600 (~30% savings).
- Q4: estimated spend per month = $9,000 (~50% savings).

SOW paragraph (one-paragraph):
"Redwood Inference will execute an 8-week Optimize pilot for BrightRoute consisting of a KV/prefix cache audit, two batching profile experiments, and a quantization evaluation across nominated model variants. Deliverables include a quantified cache-hit estimate, a recommendation matrix per model/quant tier, cost-delta worksheets, and an implementation runbook. Redwood will run tests on a 250-item prompt set provided by BrightRoute; results and artifacts will be delivered within five business days of the final testing window."

Next steps: I’ll upload the Drive folder and a HubSpot deal. If that works, I’ll send a DocuSign for the pilot acceptance (no prepayment required; credits applied on usage).

Best,
Elliot Price
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
